notes: Goal clear (one shared renderer URI); issue proposes a single canonical ui://prefab/renderer.html and says nothing on tools with different CSP. Tests go beyond the issue: identity keyed by Prefab version, delivery mode and CSP/permissions/domain/border, legacy per-tool URIs still readable. Implementing the issue's own expected behaviour fails these behaviourally, not just on names, so 3 (too broad).

Issue is precise and gives a fix (treat a name as pre-addressed only if it equals hashed_backend_name). Gold instead changes the address format to __<hash>_<name> and rejects reserved names at registration; tests check the new format, parse requiring '__', and a ValueError 'reserved for generated tool addresses'. The suggested fix fails 10 of 12 F2P tests.

Clear goal (dropped servers' tool functions must be collectable); three alternative fixes offered, so the approach is open. Tests parametrize over four caches, two of them (_wrap_body_errors, session_id_parameter_names) not named in the issue, and require release with no explicit call, so the issue's remove_tool or public forget(fn) options fail. Weak/on-callable caching of all four passes.

Issue is very clear with a runnable example, and the tests check exactly that behaviour (plus the same bug in the OpenAPI parser). The problem is a name: collection_error, test_json_schema.py imports ref_target_name, which the issue never names, so without that exact helper all 86 F2P tests in the file fail. Rubric case 2.

Issue accepts two outcomes: make the template readable or don't list it. Tests accept only 'readable', so the other outcome the issue allows fails behaviourally: 3 (too narrow). Readable solutions also need the exact sanitized keys (_top, x_y, _1id, a_) and expand_uri_template/forward_uri support, which alone would be a 2.

Problem well described, desired behaviour not: warn, raise AlreadyRegistered (hinted by the issue) or disambiguate names via __qualname__. Tests accept only one of these (warn, once per name, specific wording), so raising or renaming fails behaviourally: 3 (too narrow). On top, collection_error on the new DuplicateTaskNameWarning breaks all 175 F2P tests in the module.

Expected behaviour clear (meta['stamp'] present with db backend); storage design left open. Tests poke internals: a 'stamps' LargeBinary column holding an encoded {'stamped_headers','stamps'} dict written directly in tests, _query_task deferring a missing 'stamps' column, TaskExtended.to_dict tolerating errors. A different storage design fails most F2P tests.

Short but clear: store children in the db backend so AsyncResult.children works; schema migration not mentioned. Most F2P tests target an auto-migration the issue never asks for (SessionManager._migrate_missing_columns, patched session.inspect/logger, 'Failed to add missing column' text) and a private _query_task fallback. Only the round-trip tests are fair.

Issue is an old 'revoked task still executes?' log referring to two other issues; nothing points at the real cause (monotonic revoke stamps from another host or before reboot via mingle/statedb filling LimitedSet). Tests require a new state.merge_revoked function, LimitedSet sequence numbers, __eq__ changes, mingle sending a list. Not solvable from the text.

Very clear: catch ResourceNotFoundError in azureblockblob delete() and 404 HTTPFailure in cosmosdbsql delete(). Tests only use names that already exist in the modules and check that delete() does not raise; any reasonable catch passes. Keep.

Feature request deferring almost all detail to an external SEP. Beyond unstated module paths and names (collection_error on mcp.server.skills, mcp.shared.skills, mcp.client.extensions.skills, Client.extension), tests/docs_src/test_skills.py checks new documentation tutorial files the issue never asks for, so the tests check more than the issue: 3.

Behaviour clear (configurable SSE event limit on POST/GET/reconnect, request-scoped error), and the tests check that behaviour. They depend on unstated names and text: max_sse_event_size (the issue suggests max_event_size and leaves the name open), the exact signature order, a StreamableHttpParameters field, the snapshot 'max_sse_event_size must be positive or None', the 'SSE stream failed: ' prefix. Rubric case 2.

Fix (1) is clear: run find_invalid_x_mcp_header at registration and raise. 9 of 14 F2P tests check new docs_src.header_parameters tutorial modules (collection_error) and their HTTP behaviour, i.e. documentation the issue never asks for: 3. The remaining tests_base ones (exact message snapshot, InvalidSignature) would alone be a 2.

Issue asks to let CIMD public clients (auth method none) use the jwt-bearer grant; implementing that needs CIMD handling the server lacks, so details are open. Gold does not implement the request: it only rewords docs, comments and a client ValueError. The F2P test checks that new message text, unrelated to the issue.

Vague style question ('probably not a bug, shouldn't this be formatted like call chains?') with one example. Tests pin a large preview-only output: all arithmetic/bitwise/comparison operators, tuples/dicts/sets, generators and parenthesized scalars excluded, magic trailing comma and line-length cases. Many reasonable scopes would fail the single golden file.

Clear bug: Black crashes (AST mismatch) and should keep the type: ignore comments in place. The exact output is not specified; tests expect one shape (app # ...  /  .builder.highlighter # ...  /  .formatter_args[...]) in stable and unstable. Other valid fixes (one attribute per line, keeping the source layout) would fail.

Desired style clear for the sole-argument call case. The golden file also requires removing double parens around generators in lists, dicts, tuples, standalone statements, before trailers, and keyword/star args, plus a specific comment case. A fix scoped to the issue fails the one F2P test.

Problem is clear; the issue offers a cwd fallback (the embedded PR description) or a clear CLI error. Gold returns (None, None) and warns. The F2P test mocks find_project_root to return (None, None) and requires the exact text 'No project root could be identified' and --quiet/--config silencing. The cwd fallback described in the issue fails it.

Request is about the GitHub Action exposing whether files changed; output names undefined beyond an is_formatted example. Tests check a different place: the black CLI itself writing to $GITHUB_OUTPUT (plus a Report.write_github_outputs method). Adding outputs in action.yml, which is what the issue asks for, fails behaviourally: 3.

Clear: writing to a sys.stdout without .buffer (Jupyter OutStream) must not crash. Tests exercise the public functions with a StringIO stdout and check the output. A fallback that writes text directly passes, except the \r\n diff case also needs the newline translation TextIOWrapper did, which a minimal fix could miss. Keep.

Issue shows only the for-loop case; 'unpacking' scope is unclear. The golden file covers assignments, comprehensions, with, del and star targets, with uneven choices (comprehension 'for ((a), (b))' keeps (a, b), 'del ((a), (b))' becomes 'del (a, b)', 'with ... as ((a), (b))' keeps one pair). A reasonable implementation would differ somewhere.

One-line question about moving two helpers into another library (w3lib); nothing says what should change in scrapy. Tests check a deprecation shim conditional on w3lib that the issue doesn't ask for (and collection_error on the private _add_http_if_no_scheme, failing all 113 F2P tests): 3.

Poorly worded request for a setting to disable the media download cache. Tests check broader semantics, an LRU bound with sizes 2/0/-1 and a per-pipeline prefixed variant, so a 'disable cache' switch fails behaviourally, not just on the name MEDIA_CACHE_SIZE: 3 (too broad). Borderline with 2, worth discussing.

One-line request ('a way to propagate an exit code from a Spider'); mechanism undefined. Tests check that mechanism through unstated names: CloseSpider(error=True), a finish_reason_error stat, an error kwarg on spider_closed (existing engine tests now expect it). The behaviour (mark crawl failed, nonzero exit) is what the issue asks. Rubric case 2.

Bug and expected output are clear (redirects of retried requests must still be dupe-filtered). test_retry_redirect_dupefilter checks that behaviour fairly; the other 5 F2P tests depend on unstated names, meta['skip_dupefilter_once'] and a warning naming supports_skip_dupefilter_once. Rubric case 2.
